Distortion.what: A slightly dark, analog-style distortion with several selectable algorithms.
Distortion.sound: Warm and smooth, with the extreme highs softened by sample averaging. Aliasing is rejected better at higher sample rates (96k is a sweet spot). The Mojo and Dyno modes can curl into strange effects when slammed.
Distortion.use: Warm overdrive on bass, drums, guitars or synths when you want to pick a flavour of crunch and are happy to lose some top end.

controls.Mode: Chooses the distortion algorithm (for example Density, Drive, Spiral, Mojo, Dyno).

Edge.what: A seven-stage, high-gain hard-clipping distortion with steep filters.
Edge.sound: Bright, edgy and never smooth. Very high gain, with a distinctive tone from the filtering between stages.
Edge.use: High-gain guitar, especially direct (DI) guitar, or a hard clipper. Run at high sample rates for the best aliasing rejection.

controls.Lowpass: Cutoff of a steep lowpass, from 25k down to deep bass. Also the ultrasonic filter.
controls.Highpass: Cuts lows before the distortion to tighten it.

Dirt.what: A softer, tubier soft-clip distortion in the spirit of Edge.
Dirt.sound: Softer clipping and lower gain than Edge, with the same controls and tone-shaping filters.
Dirt.use: Guitars, especially DI guitar into a cab sim, and anything that needs gentle grit.

controls.Lowpass: Steep lowpass. Lower values keep aliasing away.

Mackity.what: The input stage of a vintage Mackie 1202 mixer.
Mackity.sound: Big, raw, spongy slam and a gleaming overload. No noise, no EQ modelling.
Mackity.use: Turning electronic music, drums or buses into a roaring wall of overloaded mixer. Not for refined recordings.

controls.In Trim: Drive into the mixer input stage.

Density3.what: The latest refinement of Density, a smooth sine-based saturation.
Density3.sound: Smooth saturation with a gentle highpass. The negative range dries up quieter regions without changing the tone.
Density3.use: Refined dirt-shaping, fattening or bringing parts forward, and subtle gating-type tone control.

controls.Density: Saturation amount. Below centre is anti-saturation, which dries up quiet parts.
controls.Highpas: Dials back saturation on heavy bass.
controls.Dry/Wet: Blend with dry. Lets bass through when the highpass is up.

ZOutputStage.what: The output clipping stage from the Emu e6400-style Z filters, as a standalone distortion.
ZOutputStage.sound: Hot, frizzy distortion on the edges of clipped sounds. Weird and twitchy.
ZOutputStage.use: Adding grind and energy to synths, drum and bass sounds or anything digital. Turn the output down.

controls.Input: Drive into the stage. Above 0.1 it distorts.
controls.Output: Level after the effect. The stage is very hot.

Density2.what: The older Density algorithm, kept exactly as it was.
Density2.sound: An alternate tone for Density, with its original quirks. Used on a hit record.
Density2.use: When you want the old Density colour.

Zoom.what: A bank of Density-like waveshapers that change peak energy while leaving loudness alone.
Zoom.sound: Subtle and hard to hear until pushed. Boosts hot peaks and cuts quieter material below centre.
Zoom.use: Mastering-style shaping of peak energy, or an overdrive or odd expander when cranked.

controls.Zoom: Amount and direction of peak reshaping. Centre is neutral.

Density.what: A Swiss Army Knife of saturation and anti-saturation, based on a sine transfer function.
Density.sound: The smoothest saturation: thick, fat and forward. Negative values thin the tone and push it back.
Density.use: Fattening, bringing parts forward or back, adding articulation to murky sounds, or huge grunge.

controls.Highpass: Filters the distorted signal so bass stays clean.

Drive.what: The angry distortion: Density's layout with a grittier tone.
Drive.sound: A nasty bark. Neither smooth nor trebly, and it hides nothing.
Drive.use: Making a bass, snare or other sound sound angry.

controls.Drive: Distortion amount. Unlike Density, it has no negative range.

Loud.what: A distortion modelled on air molecules breaking apart under extreme sound levels.
Loud.sound: Extremely nonlinear: air compresses to near solid and snaps back fast. At zero boost it acts as glue; cranked it goes completely fried.
Loud.use: Glue on a whole mix, or ferocious boosts on guitars and drums.

controls.Boost: Distortion amount. Even zero adds glue.

HardVacuum.what: Tube-style saturation with warmth and an unusual high-end control.
HardVacuum.sound: Sine-based saturation, second-harmonic warmth, and sparkly highs and searing overtones from Aura. Not a specific tube model.
HardVacuum.use: Tube-like saturation on tracks or the mix. Aura is a way to doctor tone that isn't EQ.

controls.Warmth: Second harmonic and nonlinearity, like a class A tube design. Exaggerated if pushed.
controls.Aura: Sparkly highs and hot overtones, reacting to the signal's amplitude and slope.

HighImpact.what: Distorted grit and punch without fatness.
HighImpact.sound: A raw 'dial-a-rasp' that leaves quiet samples alone, boosts mid ones a lot and walls off the loudest. Doesn't bloat.
HighImpact.use: Percussive sounds that need rasp or slam without getting fatter.

MultiBandDistortion.what: An old, gnarly two-band sound wrecker.
MultiBandDistortion.sound: Slammed, unnatural and choppy. Lowering Stable gives a Fuzz Factory-like effect.
MultiBandDistortion.use: Wrecking sounds on purpose. It isn't meant to be controllable or clean.

controls.Freqcy: Crossover between the low and high bands.
controls.H Hard: Hardness of the high band's clipping.
controls.L Hard: Hardness of the low band's clipping.
controls.Stable: Interaction between bands. Lower is more choppy and unstable.
